agents.name: Codex
agents.quote: Desktop usually hides the trace of all the commands that it runs, whereas the CLI is more verbose, but I can see a lot more things at a quick glance.

agents.name: Claude Code
agents.quote: I can just go out, and I can close my laptop, and it works, which is amazing.

history.value: Claude Code, logs analysed with her own Sniffly
history.quote: I open sourced Sniffly, a tool that analyzes Claude Code logs to help me understand my usage patterns and errors.

models.name: Claude Fable
models.quote: I feel like it's very wasteful to use uh strong models like fable to do actual implementations.

review_style.value: A second agent reviews the plan; UI work comes with screenshot evidence on the PR
review_style.quote: I give it a process: do this, and then get another to review it, and then do post-mortems.

also.quote: It can show it to me, attach to a PR, so I can approve it without having to spin up the branch associated with that PR.
Across my projects, the interruption rate is about 1 in 4 instructions. This means I still need to actively monitor the agent, rather than letting it operate autonomously.

harness.value: Her own cross-provider runner: a strong agent plans and reviews, cheap agents implement, each in a git worktree
harness.quote: I get a very strong agent to make plans and think, and then it assigns tasks to a bunch of cheaper agents to do it.

parallelism.quote: With my runner, there's no limit, so it can spin up 10 sub-agents.

history.quote: I can do like 20, 30 or like as however much money I want to spend on it.

signature.caption: Codex, Claude spawn each other
signature.why: Our pick: she built her own runner so a strong model plans and reviews while Codex and Claude agents hand work to each other.
signature.quote: That's why I built my runner, so they can do that in the same place.

archetype.why: A supervising model fans work out to cheap agents; one project logged 1,409 of them.

signature_quote.value: A lot of times, the agents make mistakes.
signature_quote.more: It's not because the agent is stupid, it's because I give them instructions not good enough.
